name: model_overview
description: Summary of the open Revit model. Pick only the sections you need: levels, grids, rooms, types, views, sheets, links, worksets, warnings, project. Long lists are cut with a note saying how many more exist and how to narrow. Use this before guessing any level, type, view or link name.

category.description: Narrow long sections to one category, e.g. Doors.

name: find_elements
description: Find elements in the host model or links. Give 1–5 queries; each can combine free text (matches name, type, mark, room, comments; Malay and English words work) with category, level, type, room, a parameter condition or in_view. Returns exact counts, up to 50 rows, a handle for reuse, and what was and was not searched. group_by counts per level/type/category/room/parameter; with sum:<parameter> it also totals a number (area, length) per group. highlight:true selects the results in Revit in the same call; zoom:true also zooms. Never say 'none' without the searched scope from the result.

text.description: Free text: name, type, mark, room or comments; Malay or English.

value.description: Not used with empty or not_empty. Give the unit, e.g. '2700 mm'.

in_view.description: Only elements visible in the active view.

group_by.description: level, type, category, room or param:<parameter name>; or two of them, e.g. ["level", "type"].

sum.description: Needs group_by. One numeric parameter to total per group, e.g. Area, Length or Volume. Each group then carries sum (display units) and without_value (elements with no value).

handle.description: Search only within the elements of an earlier handle.

name: inspect
description: Read parameters of elements (by ids, a handle or the current selection) in display units, with storage type and read-only flags; include_type adds type parameters. schedule reads a schedule's rows by name. explain_visibility says exactly why the elements are not visible in a view (view range, filters, template, workset, phase, design option, crop, hidden category or element) and how to fix each reason.

target.description: Give one of ids, handle or selection:true. Give target or schedule (at least one).

fields.description: Parameter names to read; omit for all.

schedule.description: Name of a schedule to read rows from. Give target or schedule (at least one).

view.description: View name; omit for the active view.

name: check
description: Run a standards rule set against the model: JKR naming/parameters/LOD, model health, UBBL or MS 1184 basics, BOMBA basics, documentation hygiene, grid and level alignment with links. Pick the rule_set from its list. Returns per-rule pass / fail / not_verified counts with the cited clause and a handle per failing group. not_verified means the check could not see the data (for example an unloaded link): report it and never treat it as a pass. check never changes the model.

rule_set.description: Rule set id; lookup(kind:'rules') describes each.

name: set_parameters
description: Set one parameter on many elements: target by filter, handle or ids, or give from_table (an attached table with element ids or a match field and values). Use it for every parameter value; for a type parameter set type_param and target its instances. Give the value with its unit: '2700 mm', '10 W', '0.04 A', '230 V'. Several parameters: send all the calls in one message, so they apply as one change. The change applies at once and the drafter can undo it; you get the committed result with read-back. A type parameter changes every instance of that type: say so.

target.description: Give one of filter, handle or ids. Omit when using from_table.

text.description: Free text: name, type, mark, room or comments; Malay or English.

value.description: Not used with empty or not_empty. Give the unit, e.g. '2700 mm'.

in_view.description: Only elements visible in the active view.

filter.description: A find_elements query; writes apply to the host model only.

from_table.description: Name of an attached table; use instead of target and value.

value.description: With its unit when it has one, e.g. '2700 mm'.

name: look
description: Get an image of the model to orient yourself: the active view, a named view, or a 3D view around elements (by handle or ids). mode 'multi' returns plan, 3D and elevation side by side. The drafter sees the same image. Use it to check placement and layout, never to count or measure: use find_elements and inspect for numbers.

name: run_revit_code
description: Run C# against the Revit API for jobs no other tool covers (sheets, views, tags, dimensions, renumbering, filters, elevations, modelling). Never set parameter values here: use set_parameters (raw numbers here land in internal units). Write method-body statements only; you get doc, uidoc, view and Print(obj). Do not open transactions: the host does. Allowed: Autodesk.Revit.DB and basic System types; no files, network, saving or dialogs. Changes apply at once and the drafter can undo them. Errors come back with line numbers: fix and retry. For known jobs, get the playbook with lookup first.

intent.description: One line shown to the drafter.

expected.description: How many elements you expect the code to add, modify and delete. Prefer the by-category counts: elements Revit creates along with them (viewports, title blocks, sun paths, centre lines) are only compared when you name their category.

adds_by_category.description: Revit category name to count, e.g. {"Sheets": 9, "Viewports": 9}.

name: lookup
description: Look things up instead of guessing. knowledge: JKR spec, JKR parameter rules, naming segments, Revit API members and fixes for Revit warnings, with citations. playbook: a step-by-step procedure with known traps for a job in the playbook list. rules: rule set ids for check. Meanings of JKR codes, parameters and naming must come from here, never from memory.

query.description: What to look up. Give query or id.

id.description: Exact entry, playbook or rule set id.

name: ask_user
description: Ask the drafter one question when something you need is missing or ambiguous: give 2–4 options taken from the model (for example the real level names), or a small form with fields. purpose 'project_note' proposes saving a project fact the drafter stated; it is saved only if they confirm. Never use this to ask permission for a change: changes apply at once and can be undone.

note_text.description: The project fact to save, with purpose project_note.
